newsitem.title: BULGARIA: EBRD approves participation in Bulgaria's UBB.
newsitem.headline: EBRD approves participation in Bulgaria's UBB.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) approved on Wednesday a 35 percent participation in Bulgaria's state-owned United Bulgarian Bank (UBB), the EBRD said.
"The EBRD board approved a 35 percent participation in UBB. The project is subject to signing next week," an EBRD official told Reuters.

Under the UBB privatisation plan, the Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which now holds more than 98 percent of UBB, will offer a further 35 percent to state-owned Bulbank and 30 percent to the U.S. Oppenheimer & Co, a subsidiary of Oppenheimer Group Inc.
The new acquisitions are due to be voted on at the UBB annual shareholders' meeting on July 25. After that, the three investors will be offered the same size stakes in a new $30 million share issue.

In line with the pledges to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) the government plans to privatise all six operating state-owned banks by mid-1998. The Bulgarian banking system has gone through a deep crisis.

UBB's capital currently totals 21.07 billion levs ($11.8 million). BCC, which manages state equity in local commercial banks, boosted UBB capital through $119 million of domestic bad loan bonds last year.
In line with changes in the bank's ownership, the UBB will abolish its two- tier management system comprising supervisory and executive boards and will replace it by a nine-member board of directors.

The nine-member board formed through nominees of all three major shareholders will be authorised to decide on a further capital increase through a new share issue of up to $15 million in the next two years, said the official.
The UBB was set up in 1992 through a merger of 22 smaller banking institutions and is expected to be the first privatisation project implemented by the BCC.
-- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145 ($ = 1789 Bulgarian Levs)
